errors: Mean-longitude addition for April 30: 8°16'27.10" + 29°34'9.90" = 37°50'37.00", but the page writes 37°50'37.10". This 0.10" slip propagates to April 30, May 4 and May 8 (and to May 12 and 16 on the next page), shifting those solar longitudes by +0.1". It is negligible for Vesta work.
The base of the third perturbation argument is 683 in the April 12 block but 684 in the April 26 and 30 blocks. This is probably a rounding of about 683.5; it is harmless.
The previous page lists X(April 26) = 0.8184006, whereas this page gives 0.8184008. This is a copying difference of 2e-7.
No other arithmetic errors were found. All sums, the log R values, and X, Y, Z and λ, β recompute to within one unit of the last place.
The equation of centre and the radius vector were checked roughly against e ≈ 0.01679 and agree to about 1"; the table-specific constants were not verifiable here.

results.what: Solar longitude and radius vector from tables (mean motion, equation of centre, lunar/Venus/Jupiter perturbations, nutation/aberration) for 1807 Apr 12–May 8
results.modern_name: Solar ephemeris computation from tables (Zach/Delambre-type solar tables)

results.what: Geocentric equatorial rectangular coordinates of the Sun X=R cos λ, Y=R sin λ cos ε, Z=R sin λ sin ε
results.modern_name: Ecliptic-to-equatorial rectangular transformation of the solar position

results.what: Conversion of Vesta's observed (α, δ) to (λ, β) via auxiliary angle N with tan N = tan δ / sin α, plus the logarithmic control tan λ/tan α = sin λ cos β/(sin α cos δ)
results.usually_credited_to: classical; given by Gauss in Theoria Motus (1809) art. 50

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine working computations: solar places and coordinate conversion for Gauss's well-documented 1807 Vesta orbit determinations. The methods are standard and appear in his own Theoria Motus.

checkable.asserts: 26 days of solar mean motion equals 25°37'36.58" (difference ≈ 0)
The April 30 mean longitude sum is 37°50'37.00", not 37.10" (result ≈ 0)
Ecliptic longitude of Vesta on Apr 12 ≈ 175.881131° (175°52'52.07")
log cos ε ≈ 9.9625167 and log sin ε ≈ 9.6000696, the constants implicit in the second and fourth log columns

transcription_corrections: In the April 12 coordinate conversion, the first entry of the middle column is 8,3042046 (log tan α), not 9,3042046; 0.5531998 + 8.3042046 = 8.8574044.
In the April 26 radius vector 1,0071382 and the April 12 value 1,0033287, the last two digits are overwritten corrections in the manuscript.
The header at top centre reads 'Litt. C' (cf. 'Lett. C' on the previous page). The faint marginal note at top left (written like 'Mo nath') is likely 'Monath'.
